title: Software's selloff, part 2: 9 links that explain who got hit, and whyBILL jumped 12%. Is the seat-based SaaS model actually broken?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Application software kept bleeding. JFrog fell 5.9%, HubSpot and  
GitLab about 5.6% each, and DocuSign 5.1% as investors re-priced  
seat-based subscription models. The exception: BILL jumped 12% on a  
report that TPG is nearing a take-private deal. Here's who got hit,  
and why one name went the other way.  
  
Here is the rundown, drawn from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. BILL (BILL)\*\* — BILL jumped +12.22% to $64.67 in Tuesday's  
regular session from Monday's close of $57.63, touching a 52-week high  
and briefly triggering a volatility halt. Catalyst: the Financial  
Times reported that TPG is leading an investor consortium close to a  
take-private deal for BILL, possibly within days and at a premium;  
neither party has confirmed.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-bill-holdings-bill-stock-up-12-22-today-39923/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-bill-holdings-bill-stock-up-12-22-today-39923/)  
  
\*\*2. JFrog (FROG)\*\* — FROG dropped from a previous close of $109.94 to  
$103.47, a -5.89% move, during Tuesday's regular session after  
premarket had ticked slightly higher. No verified news or fundamental  
catalyst found; the pullback is likely profit-taking after a +52% run  
off the November 5 close, with today's decline only about 1.5x the  
stock's 3.9% average absolute daily move over the last 60 sessions.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-jfrog-ltd-frog-stock-down-5-89-today-39883/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-jfrog-ltd-frog-stock-down-5-89-today-39883/)  
  
\*\*3. HubSpot (HUBS)\*\* — HubSpot shares fell -5.58%, dropping from  
Monday's close of $231.98 to $219.03 during Tuesday's regular session,  
as of 11:02 a.m. ET. The decline was not company-specific: a  
sector-wide de-rating of seat-based application software accelerated  
as investors positioned for Anthropic's IPO expected to price  
Wednesday, with AI agents seen threatening per-user subscription  
models.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-hubspot-inc-hubs-stock-down-5-58-today-39886/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-hubspot-inc-hubs-stock-down-5-58-today-39886/)  
  
\*\*4. GitLab (GTLB)\*\* — GitLab (GTLB) dropped from a $47.33 close to  
$44.70, a -5.56% decline, during Tuesday's regular session as of late  
morning in New York. The decline was driven by a broad selloff in  
application-software shares as investors reassessed seat-based  
subscription models that AI tools may make less necessary at  
customers; no GitLab-specific news or filing accompanied the move.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-gitlab-inc-gtlb-stock-down-5-45-today-39890/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-gitlab-inc-gtlb-stock-down-5-45-today-39890/)  
  
\*\*5. Guidewire Software (GWRE)\*\* — Guidewire Software fell -5.36%, or  
\-$8.31, to $146.68 from Monday's close of $154.99, with the decline  
occurring during regular U.S. market hours. The move was driven by a  
broad software selloff rather than company news: the iShares Expanded  
Tech-Software ETF dropped -4.4%, Salesforce -9.6% and Workday -5.5%,  
as AI-trade jitters ahead of Nvidia's earnings and a 10-year Treasury  
yield above 5% hit...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-guidewire-software-gwre-stock-down-5-31-today-39885/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-guidewire-software-gwre-stock-down-5-31-today-39885/)  
  
\*\*6. Qualys (QLYS)\*\* — Qualys (QLYS) dropped -5.24%, sliding from  
Monday's close of $182.01 to $172.48, with the move occurring during  
Tuesday's regular session as of 11:04 a.m. ET. The decline is  
sector-driven: a broad software and cybersecurity selloff, with no  
company-specific release or filing from Qualys, as traders cut risk  
ahead of Nvidia's earnings and a 10-year Treasury yield near 5.14%  
weighs on richly valued software.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-qualys-qlys-stock-down-5-24-today-39897/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-qualys-qlys-stock-down-5-24-today-39897/)  
  
\*\*7. DocuSign (DOCU)\*\* — DocuSign fell -5.11% to $75.74, down -$4.08  
from Monday's $79.82 close, with the bulk of the decline coming during  
regular-session trading after premarket losses of only about -1%. The  
driver is a sector-wide application-software selloff, not company  
news: investors are questioning seat-based subscription economics as  
AI tools cut customer headcount, undermining per-user pricing models.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-docusign-inc-docu-stock-down-5-11-today-39882/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-docusign-inc-docu-stock-down-5-11-today-39882/)  
  
\*\*8. Netskope (NTSK)\*\* — Netskope (NTSK) dropped -4.94%, sliding from  
a $21.86 close on Nov. 16 to $20.78 in regular-session trading on Nov.  
17, with the decline deepening through the morning after an $21.81  
open. No verified news or fundamental catalyst found for the session:  
no company release, filing or new analyst action accompanied the move,  
which extends a de-rating that began with Morgan Stanley's Nov. 13  
downgrade to...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-netskope-ntsk-stock-down-5-99-today-39892/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-netskope-ntsk-stock-down-5-99-today-39892/)  
  
\*\*9. Similarweb (SMWB)\*\* — Similarweb reported third quarter 2026  
revenue of $83.0 million, up 15.6% year over year and above its  
guidance range, with growth accelerating versus the prior year.  
Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) came in at $0.10, beating  
the $0.08 consensus estimate, while non-GAAP operating profit more  
than doubled to $10.1 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/similarweb-smwb-posts-15-6-revenue-growth-and-achieves-first-positive-gaap-eps-40048/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/similarweb-smwb-posts-15-6-revenue-growth-and-achieves-first-positive-gaap-eps-40048/)  
  
Is the seat-based SaaS model actually broken?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 17) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
